# REST API: Task tokens

<!-- Generated by scripts/generate_reference.py from openapi.json. Do not edit by hand:
run `uv run python scripts/generate_reference.py` and commit the result. -->

These routes of the platform API come from its [OpenAPI document](../openapi.json); [The REST API as a contract](../rest-api.md) says what Lakana promises about them.

## `GET /api/v1/task-tokens`

List the live task tokens

Lists the task tokens that are neither revoked nor expired, newest first (or in the order `sort` and `order` ask for), each with the principal it signs in as, its environment and asset scope, its dates and, for a token a worker minted for a task, the run, job and asset. The token values are never included. Needs the `ADMIN` role on the instance; a task or CI token is refused. The cursor of the next page is in the `X-Next-Cursor` response header and is absent on the last page. An `environment` no token names gives an empty list, not a 404. Answers 422 for an unknown `sort` or `order`, or a cursor this list did not issue in this order; send the same sort with every page.

Parameters:

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `environment` | query | no | text or null | Only the tokens of this environment; every environment when left out. |
| `limit` | query | no | whole number | Most tokens returned (1 to 200). |
| `cursor` | query | no | text or null | The `X-Next-Cursor` of the previous page; send the same `environment`. |
| `sort` | query | no | text or null | What the list is sorted by: `issued` (the default), `environment`, `purpose` (the job, else the asset; one minted by hand last), `acts_as` or `expires`. |
| `order` | query | no | text or null | `asc` or `desc`; by default `desc` for `issued`, `asc` for the others. |
| `authorization` | header | no | text or null | The credential: `Bearer <token>` with a personal access token, task token or CI token. Without it, the web interface's session cookie counts instead. |

Answers:

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| `200` | Successful Response | list of `TaskTokenOut` |
| `401` | Not signed in: the token or browser session is missing, wrong, expired or revoked; an ended session says why in `reason`. | `ErrorOut` |
| `403` | Signed in, but not allowed to do this; the message says why and what to do next. | `ErrorOut` |
| `422` | Validation Error | `HTTPValidationError` |

## `POST /api/v1/task-tokens`

Mint a task token

Mints a short-lived token that acts for a principal in one environment, limited to the assets named in the request. The answer holds the token's value, shown this once. Needs `MINT_TASK_TOKEN` on the instance; minting a token for a principal other than yourself also needs the `ADMIN` role (403 otherwise). Answers 404 when the principal or environment does not exist.

Parameters:

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `authorization` | header | no | text or null | The credential: `Bearer <token>` with a personal access token, task token or CI token. Without it, the web interface's session cookie counts instead. |

Request body (application/json, required): `TaskTokenMintIn`

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `principal` | text | yes |  |
| `environment` | text | yes |  |
| `asset_scope` | list of text | yes |  |
| `ttl_seconds` | whole number | yes |  |

Answers:

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| `201` | Successful Response | `TaskTokenMintOut` |
| `401` | Not signed in: the token or browser session is missing, wrong, expired or revoked; an ended session says why in `reason`. | `ErrorOut` |
| `403` | Signed in, but not allowed to do this; the message says why and what to do next. | `ErrorOut` |
| `404` | What the request names does not exist, or the caller may not know that it does. | `ErrorOut` |
| `422` | Validation Error | `HTTPValidationError` |

Answer fields: `TaskTokenMintOut`

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `key_id` | text | yes |  |
| `token` | text | yes |  |

## `DELETE /api/v1/task-tokens/{key_id}`

Revoke a task token

Ends the token before it expires. Revoking a token that is revoked already changes nothing. Needs `MINT_TASK_TOKEN` on the instance. An administrator may revoke any token and gets 404 for an unknown key id; anyone else may revoke only a token minted for themselves over REST and gets 403 otherwise, also for an unknown key id, so that key ids cannot be probed.

Parameters:

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `key_id` | path | yes | text | The task token's key_id. |
| `authorization` | header | no | text or null | The credential: `Bearer <token>` with a personal access token, task token or CI token. Without it, the web interface's session cookie counts instead. |

Answers:

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| `204` | Successful Response | none |
| `401` | Not signed in: the token or browser session is missing, wrong, expired or revoked; an ended session says why in `reason`. | `ErrorOut` |
| `403` | Signed in, but not allowed to do this; the message says why and what to do next. | `ErrorOut` |
| `404` | What the request names does not exist, or the caller may not know that it does. | `ErrorOut` |
| `422` | Validation Error | `HTTPValidationError` |
